candidates.node_relation: Governed enterprise data layer for AI applications and agents; enables models to operate near customer data with governance, security, and privacy controls.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Cloud data platform / enterprise data management
candidates.theme_relation: AI workloads require high-quality, permissioned, structured and unstructured enterprise data; Snowflake is a second-order beneficiary if AI deployment shifts from model experimentation to governed enterprise production.
candidates.why_include: Snowflake directly maps to the bottleneck hypothesis: enterprises often cannot deploy AI without clean, governed, permissioned data. Recent partnerships with model providers and Cortex AI suggest Snowflake is positioning itself as the control plane where enterprise AI apps and agents access governed data rather than moving data into isolated AI systems.

candidates.next_evidence: Track Pro Plus AI / AI platform annual contract value, attach rates, renewal uplift, workflow expansion, margin impact from AI inference costs, and whether customers are using agents in production rather than demos.
candidates.node_relation: Workflow execution and change-management layer that connects AI agents to business processes, data fabric, approvals, and enterprise operating systems.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Enterprise workflow automation / IT service management / AI platform
candidates.theme_relation: If AI value moves from chatbots to autonomous workflow execution, ServiceNow is a plausible chokepoint because it owns operational workflows across IT, HR, customer service, security, and enterprise service management.
candidates.why_include: ServiceNow is not just selling AI features; it is trying to embed agentic AI into workflow data fabric, enterprise search, and governed autonomous work. Its acquisitions of Moveworks and data.world strengthen exposure to enterprise assistant/search and data catalog/governance chokepoints.

candidates.next_evidence: Verify monetization of AI-agent identity products, adoption by major AI application vendors, incremental ARR from governance/security modules, competitive positioning versus Microsoft Entra, CyberArk/Palo Alto, and cloud-native IAM tools.
candidates.node_relation: Permissioning, identity, and access-control layer for AI agents, non-human identities, cross-application authorization, and auditability.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Identity and access management / identity governance
candidates.theme_relation: AI agents need controlled access to enterprise apps, files, calendars, SaaS systems, and databases. Identity governance may become a hidden chokepoint as enterprises deploy agents with autonomous permissions.
candidates.why_include: Okta is a less obvious second-order beneficiary: AI agents increase the number and complexity of identities that must be discovered, authorized, governed, monitored, and revoked. Okta’s Cross App Access and agent identity products map directly to permission and governance bottlenecks.

candidates.theme_relation: As enterprises move AI agents into production, they need to observe model behavior, latency, cost, hallucination/error patterns, permissions, and downstream system effects; observability becomes a deployment chokepoint.
candidates.why_include: Datadog is a second-order AI infrastructure beneficiary not tied to chips. Its LLM Observability, AI Agent Monitoring, AI Agents Console, GPU Monitoring, Sensitive Data Scanner, and AI Guard products address production reliability and governance gaps that can block enterprise AI rollout.

candidates.why_include: MongoDB’s AI relevance is indirect but plausible: AI applications need context stores, semantic search, application data, and retrieval infrastructure. memory_update.text: SNOW should remain a core candidate for the enterprise AI data layer because governed enterprise data access is a direct bottleneck for AI agents and production GenAI apps.
NOW maps to the workflow automation/action layer of enterprise AI; prioritize evidence around AI attach rate, Pro Plus AI ACV, and agentic workflow deployment quality.
OKTA is a less obvious but potentially important second-order beneficiary because AI agents create non-human identity, cross-app authorization, and permission-governance problems.
DDOG is relevant to production AI because observability, LLM monitoring, agent evaluation, cost monitoring, and incident response are deployment bottlenecks after prototypes move into real workflows.

MDB is a plausible AI application data-layer candidate via integrated operational data, vector search, semantic search, and RAG/agent context infrastructure, but monetization evidence remains less direct.

Important companies not included due to the 5-candidate cap but worth later passes: CRM for Agentforce and Informatica acquisition, PANW for CyberArk/agent identity security exposure, ORCL/SAP/MSFT for enterprise system-of-record control, ESTC for search/RAG/security observability, and PATH for robotic process automation.

node: Enterprise AI software, data integration, governance, and automation layer
summary: Expanded universe for the AI enterprise deployment layer, emphasizing underappreciated chokepoints around governed enterprise data, AI agent workflow execution, permissions/identity, vector-search-enabled application data, and LLM/agent observability. This is research support only, not a buy/sell list. The highest-relevance candidates for this pass are Snowflake, ServiceNow, Okta, Datadog, and MongoDB because each maps to a practical deployment bottleneck: governed data access, workflow orchestration, identity/permission control, production monitoring/evaluation, or AI application data infrastructure.
